items.text: Vertical software, SaaS
Keeping customers gets you the meeting. Growing them sets the price.

Over twelve months the listed software index fell from 5.7 to 3.2 times revenue, while the median private software transaction moved from 4.2 to 4.0. Private prices held. The gap between what owners expect and what clears is now the most cited reason deals fail.

sections.name: The retention figure is the median. The end market is the argument.

items.text: What a buyer reads
The retention figure is the median. The end market is the argument.
A buyer will recompute your retention from your own records, and then ask who your customers are and who is buying them.
Median private SaaS transaction, enterprise value to trailing revenue, Q2 2026
Above the listed index median of 3.2 times in the same quarter. Vertical software was 54 percent of deal volume.
Median net revenue retention at $3M to $20M of recurring revenue
With 91 percent gross retention and 15 percent growth. Meeting the median does not set a business apart.
The same measure, from billing-platform data
A different population of companies. A second panel puts median gross retention at 84 percent, down from 88.
Broken letters of intent where the earnings were not what was presented
Twice the 2023 rate of 10.6 percent.

No named publisher measures what growth, margin or preparation adds to the price of a private software company. The published premiums are for listed companies. Anyone putting a specific multiple on preparation is quoting their own marketing, and we will not.

Software Equity Group, Q2 2026 SaaS M&A and Public Market Report, August 5, 2026. SaaS Capital, annual survey of more than 1,000 private B2B SaaS companies, April 24, 2026. ChartMogul, December 10, 2025. Benchmarkit, 2026. The retention figures measure different populations and are shown side by side, not averaged. A lower-middle-market deal platform’s published study of broken letters of intent, January 27, 2026: seventy-five broken letters across eight buyer types and eight industries, with 2023 comparisons from the same series. The percentages are separate reported categories and are not summed here.

items.text: What the review covers
The questions a buyer’s quality of earnings will ask, answered on your side of the table.
This is non-attest preparation. It shows you what a buyer’s quality of earnings is likely to find, while there is still time to act on it.
Earnings, traced
Revenue reconciled to bank deposits, and reported earnings tied to the records behind them.
Every adjustment, marked
Each add-back you or your adviser proposes is marked supported or unsupported, with the document that decides it.
Customers and payers
Concentration, retention and contract terms, read the way a buyer will read them.
Contracts and licenses
Assignability, change-of-control terms, and the compliance items a buyer’s counsel will ask about.
A findings report and workbook
What was found, what it affects, and what to fix first. Yours to keep. See the full review.
Come prepared.

Capital Row is the M&A firm that reads your numbers the way a buyer will, before you go to market. Every figure traced to a source document, every adjustment marked supported or unsupported, and the findings are yours to keep.
Request a Pre-Market Assessment
